selected_title: When Is History Long Enough? Conditional Quantile Models versus Historical Rules for Peak Net-Position Limits
alternative_title_for_user: Hard to Beat: Historical Rules versus Conditional Quantile Models for Peak Net-Position Limits

clauses.text: Historical rules provide a demanding benchmark for conditional forecasts of peak net positions in the examined dealer records.
clauses.limit: This is a statement about the tested records and finite procedures, not every conditional model.

clauses.text: The prespecified simulation comparisons support the registered short-history disadvantage and long-history advantage predictions.
clauses.limit: The selected coordinate is descriptive; method-specific follow-ups cannot distinguish coefficient normalization.

clauses.text: The FX history comparisons have identified crossings and one left-censored crossing.
clauses.limit: Known-period reuse, nonmonotone curves and pooled-versus-fixed-horizon objects prevent a universal history threshold.

clauses.text: Allowing stronger shrinkage in the specified simulation menu reduces its short-history median loss disadvantage.
clauses.limit: This does not prove that every increase in penalty improves loss or isolate a unique estimation-cost mechanism.

clauses.text: Existing weekly diagnostics show both selection losses and remaining losses within the tested finite menu.
clauses.limit: Retrospective sensitivity and evaluation hindsight are diagnostic rather than deployable selection.

clauses.text: The relative cost of a conditional limit also depends on the stated reserve, breach and exceedance charges.
clauses.limit: The fixed cost grid has local exceptions and is not a measured trading-policy benefit.

clauses.text: The existing higher-quantile extension remains undetermined.
clauses.limit: Failures and missing outcomes cannot be promoted to success.

unifying_interpretation: History, finite-menu shrinkage, selection and cost preferences jointly organize the examined comparisons; the unique causal estimation-cost account is not identified.
design_boundary: Existing CFTC W52/W260 outcomes have already been inspected in B and WP0. New W520 results have not been run; preregistration must distinguish a new source-based check from an untouched holdout claim.
